body: Porcelain shaping, 2026-09-19. Ben proposes provenance <node> <create|update|archive> with get as the default. He corrects delete to archive. After confirming that the caller supplies the new record ID, he accepts the consistent target-ID interpretation and requests: great. update provenance and then we can continue. The accepted grammar is provenance <id> [get|create|update|archive]. Create names the new record and requires its kind explicitly; existing-record actions resolve the kind from the ID. Parent relationships are supplied separately. CLI and MCP share the action names. Node reading retains child selection, depth, returned-kind filters, and grounding and impact views. Root search remains available. This replaces noun-first record-family authoring and the prior verb-first explicit get spelling. Archive reuses the existing lifecycle policy. Exact mutation options, collection add/remove/replace behavior, identifier ambiguity handling, and read-view details remain open.

Porcelain shaping, 2026-09-19. Ben accepts retaining prime for CLI project orientation: yep. Prime is goated. He explicitly leaves MCP exposure open: Not sure if an MCP server needs it though. Not sure. The contents of prime and its possible MCP tool or resource representation remain undecided.
prime doesn't tell an agent about the project. It tells an agent about Provenance

Porcelain shaping, 2026-09-19. Ben agrees to retain prime for CLI and omit a separate MCP prime tool. Shared Provenance guidance reaches CLI agents through prime and MCP agents through server instructions and tool descriptions. This is an accepted transport-specific exception to matching command names. MCP client delivery details do not imply that every host automatically injects all guidance. Exact guidance content and host integration details remain open.

Porcelain shaping, 2026-09-19. Ben agrees to one check entry point with selectable graph-validity, statement-quality, and coverage checks, then asks whether it should default to all. The accepted command keeps these findings distinct: absent implementation or verification does not make a Rule record invalid. The default selection, exact flags, and node-scoped checking remain open.

Porcelain shaping, 2026-09-19. Ben accepts all three check categories by default with great. A bare check runs graph-validity, statement-quality, and coverage checks. Explicit selectors narrow the set; multiple selectors choose their union. No separate all selector is needed. Output summarizes each category and actionable findings. An unavailable check is not reported as passed. Existing failure policy still applies; missing bindings do not automatically invalidate a record or force failure. Coverage inspects bindings rather than executing the project test suite.

Porcelain shaping, 2026-09-19. After reviewing OpenCode V2 Code Mode, Ben accepts API and SQL as sufficient general-access commands: ageed. API and SQL is enough. The accepted recommendation leaves program execution with the agent host, which can compose Provenance operations, and defers a Provenance-hosted SDK execution command. The official V2 MCP documentation says Code Mode is enabled by default; the inspected local CodeMode package explains progressive discovery, tool composition, and keeping intermediate results outside model context. SQL read/write policy, exposed query schema, revision support, and API discovery details remain open.
yes sql absolutely must be readonly

Porcelain shaping, 2026-09-19. After discussing the cost of resolving a node ID to its kind, Ben accepts the explanation and the previously proposed domain actions: ok fair enough, agreed about your other actions. The proposed examples were question answer, topic claim/release, and Requirement submit, expressed as provenance <id> <action>. These actions use existing domain operations and apply only to supported record kinds. The type-resolution discussion supports retaining node-first grammar; it does not establish an end-to-end latency target or mandate a new index.
I think based on that it's important for the agent to be able to read discussion enough that they should be first class.

Ben accepts the proposed discussion grammar with: yep makes sense. The CLI uses provenance <node-id> discussions to find attached discussions, provenance <discussion-id> to read a discussion and its messages, provenance <node-id> discuss to start a discussion, and provenance <discussion-id> reply to add a reply. MCP uses the same actions with structured target arguments; get is the explicit action for the default CLI read. Reads are bounded and provide a way to fetch further messages. Exact inputs, message order, and pagination syntax remain open.

Ben accepts scope-wide and node-scoped discussion lists with: agreed. Both forms default to active discussions. The CLI uses provenance discussions and provenance <node-id> discussions, with --status resolved and --status all for other selections. MCP exposes discussions with optional parent and status arguments. Lists include discussion ID, parent ID, status, and a short opening-message excerpt, with bounded results and pagination. Active refers to Discussion lifecycle status, not recent activity or the containing Thread status.
yep. I think these are all patches so in spirit they should not be destructive

Ben answers yes to accepting an existing relationship addition or an absent relationship removal as a successful no-op. The accepted recommendation retains errors for invalid targets and forbidden relationships. Existing validation and concurrency rules still apply.
yep perfect. Very easy for a human to understand. Just need to make sure that's what our API currently supports

Ben accepts the proposed gh api-style interface with: yessir. The api command uses public API paths, defaults to GET, accepts an explicit method, and reads a request body from a file or standard input. Provenance handles the configured repository, scope, and credentials. Existing mutation preconditions still apply. Built-in discovery describes routes, methods, request inputs, and response shapes from the operation catalog. MCP api exposes path, method, query, headers, and body as structured arguments. Discovery spelling remains open.
yep perfect. We already use SQLite FYI

I'd prefer readable rendered text if at all possible. For surfaces consumed by agents, I'd really like for us to be conscious of token usage. What is best practice here? what does the MCP standard recommend?

Ben accepts the output recommendation with: sounds good to me. CLI output defaults to readable rendering with explicit JSON access. MCP offers readable content and schema-defined data; the JSON text fallback policy requires compatibility checks against supported hosts. List and search views stay compact. Record and discussion reads provide the requested detail. Evaluation considers token use and task success. The exact MCP wire-format choice remains open.
ids should never ever match. they must be unique across the system

the agent is probably going to come back and say something like "There's is nothing to force uniqueness in ids" tbh it can be a pivot table on the sqllite DB and a provenance check thing to verify uniqueness. It'll make lookup way faster too
no.. uniqueness id across repositories is totally unecessary. CLI basically always queries in repo scope
